import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import type { Ctx, Page } from './ctx';
import { getUnit } from './data';
import { loadProgress, loadSettings, openUnit, saveProgress, saveSettings } from './engine/store';
import type { Progress, Settings } from './types';
import Dashboard from './components/Dashboard';
import Course from './components/Course';
import LessonView from './components/LessonView';
import { GrammarPage, MyProgress, ReviewPage, SettingsPage, VocabularyPage } from './components/Pages';

const NAV: [Page, string][] = [['dashboard', 'Dashboard'], ['course', 'My Course'], ['progress', 'My Progress'], ['review', 'Review'], ['vocabulary', 'Vocabulary'], ['grammar', 'Grammar'], ['settings', 'Settings']];

export default function App() {
  const [progress, setProgress] = useState<Progress>(loadProgress);
  const [settings, setSettingsState] = useState<Settings>(loadSettings);
  const [view, setView] = useState<{ page: Page; unit?: string; tab?: string }>({ page: 'dashboard' });
  useEffect(() => saveProgress(progress), [progress]);
  useEffect(() => { window.scrollTo(0, 0); }, [view.page, view.unit]);
  const ctx: Ctx = {
    progress, update: f => setProgress(f), settings, setSettings: s => { setSettingsState(s); saveSettings(s); },
    go: (page, unit, tab) => {
      const u = getUnit(unit);
      if (page === 'lesson' && u && progress.currentUnit !== u.id) setProgress(p => openUnit(p, u.level, u.id, u.title));
      setView({ page, unit, tab });
    }
  };
  const unit = getUnit(view.unit);
  const active = view.page === 'lesson' ? 'course' : view.page;
  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen">
      <header className="sticky top-0 z-10 border-b border-slate-200 bg-white">
        <div className="mx-auto flex max-w-5xl flex-wrap items-center gap-x-6 px-4">
          <button className="min-h-[48px] text-lg font-bold text-brand-600" onClick={() => ctx.go('dashboard')}>ENGLISH PATH</button>
          <nav aria-label="Main" className="-mx-4 flex flex-1 gap-1 overflow-x-auto px-4">{NAV.map(([p, l]) => <button key={p} aria-current={active === p ? 'page' : undefined} onClick={() => ctx.go(p)} className={`min-h-[48px] shrink-0 border-b-2 px-3 text-sm font-medium ${active === p ? 'border-brand-600 text-brand-600' : 'border-transparent text-slate-600 hover:text-slate-900'}`}>{l}</button>)}</nav>
        </div>
      </header>
      <main className="mx-auto max-w-5xl px-4 py-6">
        {view.page === 'dashboard' && <Dashboard ctx={ctx} />}
        {view.page === 'course' && <Course ctx={ctx} />}
        {view.page === 'lesson' && (unit ? <LessonView unit={unit} tab={view.tab ?? 'objectives'} ctx={ctx} /> : <p>Unit not found.</p>)}
        {view.page === 'progress' && <MyProgress ctx={ctx} />}
        {view.page === 'review' && <ReviewPage ctx={ctx} />}
        {view.page === 'vocabulary' && <VocabularyPage ctx={ctx} />}
        {view.page === 'grammar' && <GrammarPage ctx={ctx} />}
        {view.page === 'settings' && <SettingsPage ctx={ctx} />}
      </main>
    </div>
  );
}

import type { Progress, Settings } from './types';
export type Page = 'dashboard' | 'course' | 'progress' | 'review' | 'vocabulary' | 'grammar' | 'settings' | 'lesson';
export interface Ctx {
  progress: Progress; update: (f: (p: Progress) => Progress) => void;
  settings: Settings; setSettings: (s: Settings) => void;
  go: (page: Page, unitId?: string, tab?: string) => void;
}

export type Level = 'A1' | 'A2' | 'B1' | 'B2' | 'C1' | 'C2';
export type ExType = 'multiple-choice' | 'fill-blank' | 'word-order' | 'true-false' | 'matching' | 'sentence-transformation' | 'short-answer' | 'reading-comprehension';
export type Answer = number | boolean | string | string[] | Record<string, string>;

export interface Exercise {
  id: string; type: ExType; instructions: string; prompt: string;
  passage?: string;            // reading-comprehension
  options?: string[];          // multiple-choice, reading-comprehension (answer = index)
  words?: string[];            // word-order (answer = correct string[])
  pairs?: [string, string][];  // matching
  answer?: Answer;             // expected answer
  accept?: string[];           // alternative accepted texts (fill-blank, transformation)
  rubric?: string;             // open types: guidance instead of auto-grading
  feedback: string;
}
export interface Vocab { word: string; translation: string; pron: string; stress?: string }
export interface Unit {
  id: string; level: Level; unitNumber: number; title: string; subtitle: string;
  objectives: string[]; communicativeGoal: string;
  grammar: { title: string; explanation: string[]; forms: { label: string; lines: string[] }[] };
  vocabulary: Vocab[]; examples: { en: string; es: string }[];
  dialogue: { speaker: string; text: string; es: string }[];
  listening: { script: { speaker: string; text: string }[]; audioUrl?: string; questions: Exercise[] };
  reading: { title: string; text: string; questions: Exercise[] };
  speaking: { prompt: string; tasks: string[] };
  writing: { prompt: string; rubric: string[]; model: string };
  pronunciation: { items: { word: string; ipa: string; stress: string }[]; tips: string[] };
  exercises: Exercise[]; assessment: Exercise[]; review: string[];
}
export interface Score { best: number; last: number; attempts: number; date: string }
export interface Progress {
  currentLevel: Level; currentUnit: string | null;
  completed: string[]; reviewUnits: string[];
  scores: Record<string, Score>;
  practice: Record<string, string[]>; // unitId -> exercise ids answered correctly
  savedVocab: string[];               // "unitId|word"
  activity: { at: string; text: string }[];
  lastActivity: string | null;
}
export interface Settings { showTranslations: boolean }

import type { Answer, Unit } from '../types';
import { grade, pct, PASS, studyTip } from '../engine/grade';
import { ExerciseSet, correctText, showAnswer } from './ExerciseView';
import type { Ctx } from '../ctx';
import { recordAssessment } from '../engine/store';

export function ResultView({ unit, answers, onRetake, ctx }: { unit: Unit; answers: Record<string, Answer>; onRetake: () => void; ctx: Ctx }) {
  const rows = unit.assessment.map(ex => ({ ex, ok: grade(ex, answers[ex.id]) === true }));
  const right = rows.filter(r => r.ok).length, score = pct(right, rows.length), passed = score >= PASS;
  return (
    <div className="space-y-4">
      <div className="card text-center">
        <p className="muted">Final assessment Â· {unit.title}</p>
        <p className="my-1 text-5xl font-bold text-brand-600">{score}%</p>
        <span className={`inline-block rounded-full px-4 py-1 text-sm font-bold text-white ${passed ? 'bg-emerald-700' : 'bg-amber-700'}`}>{passed ? 'COMPLETED' : 'REVIEW'}</span>
        <p className="mt-3">{right} correct Â· {rows.length - right} incorrect</p>
        <p className="muted mt-2">{studyTip(score)}</p>
        <div className="mt-4 flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-2"><button className="btn" onClick={onRetake}>Retake assessment</button><button className="btn btn2" onClick={() => ctx.go('lesson', unit.id, 'grammar')}>Review grammar</button><button className="btn btn2" onClick={() => ctx.go('course')}>Back to course</button></div>
      </div>
      <div className="card"><h3 className="mb-3 text-lg font-semibold">Explanations</h3>
        <ol className="space-y-3">{rows.map(({ ex, ok }, i) => (
          <li key={ex.id} className={`rounded-lg border p-3 ${ok ? 'border-emerald-200 bg-emerald-50' : 'border-red-200 bg-red-50'}`}>
            <p className="font-medium">{i + 1}. {ex.prompt} <span className="muted">({ok ? 'correct' : 'incorrect'})</span></p>
            {!ok && <p className="text-sm">Your answer: {showAnswer(ex, answers[ex.id])} Â· Correct: <b>{correctText(ex)}</b></p>}
            <p className="text-sm">{ex.feedback}</p></li>))}</ol></div>
    </div>
  );
}

export default function AssessmentView({ unit, ctx }: { unit: Unit; ctx: Ctx }) {
  const [answers, setAnswers] = useState<Record<string, Answer> | null>(null);
  const [run, setRun] = useState(0);
  const prev = ctx.progress.scores[unit.id];
  if (answers) return <ResultView unit={unit} answers={answers} ctx={ctx} onRetake={() => { setAnswers(null); setRun(run + 1); }} />;
  const finish = (a: Record<string, Answer>) => {
    const right = unit.assessment.filter(ex => grade(ex, a[ex.id]) === true).length, score = pct(right, unit.assessment.length);
    ctx.update(p => recordAssessment(p, unit.id, unit.title, score, score >= PASS));
    setAnswers(a);
  };
  return (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <div className="card"><h3 className="text-lg font-semibold">Final assessment</h3>
        <p className="muted">{unit.assessment.length} questions. Score {PASS}% or more to complete the unit; below {PASS}% the unit goes to Review.{prev ? ` Best score so far: ${prev.best}%.` : ''}</p></div>
      <ExerciseSet key={run} exercises={unit.assessment} mode="test" onFinish={finish} finishLabel="Submit assessment" />
    </div>
  );
}

import type { Ctx } from '../ctx';
import type { Level } from '../types';
import { LEVELS, UNITS_PER_LEVEL, unitsOf } from '../data';
import ProgressBar from './ProgressBar';

export const levelStatus = (ctx: Ctx, l: Level) => {
  const us = unitsOf(l), done = us.filter(u => ctx.progress.completed.includes(u.id)).length;
  if (!us.length) return 'Content coming soon';
  if (done === UNITS_PER_LEVEL) return 'Completed';
  return done > 0 || us.some(u => ctx.progress.scores[u.id]) ? 'In progress' : 'Available';
};
export const LevelSelector = ({ ctx }: { ctx: Ctx }) => (
  <div role="tablist" className="-mx-4 flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto px-4 pb-2">{LEVELS.map(l => (
    <button key={l.id} role="tab" aria-selected={ctx.progress.currentLevel === l.id} onClick={() => ctx.update(p => ({ ...p, currentLevel: l.id }))} className={`min-h-[48px] shrink-0 rounded-lg border px-4 text-left ${ctx.progress.currentLevel === l.id ? 'border-brand-600 bg-brand-600 text-white' : 'border-slate-300 bg-white'}`}>
      <span className="block font-semibold">{l.id}</span><span className="block text-xs">{l.name}</span></button>))}</div>);

export function UnitList({ ctx, level }: { ctx: Ctx; level: Level }) {
  const us = unitsOf(level);
  return (<ul className="space-y-3">{Array.from({ length: UNITS_PER_LEVEL }, (_, i) => i + 1).map(n => { const u = us.find(x => x.unitNumber === n);
    if (!u) return <li key={n} className="card opacity-60"><p className="font-semibold">Unit {n}</p><p className="muted">Content arrives in a later batch.</p></li>;
    const s = ctx.progress.scores[u.id], st = ctx.progress.completed.includes(u.id) ? 'COMPLETED' : ctx.progress.reviewUnits.includes(u.id) ? 'REVIEW' : s ? 'IN PROGRESS' : 'NOT STARTED';
    return (<li key={u.id}><button className="card w-full text-left hover:border-brand-600" onClick={() => ctx.go('lesson', u.id, 'objectives')}>
      <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-3"><div><p className="muted">Unit {n}</p><p className="text-lg font-semibold">{u.title}</p><p className="muted">{u.subtitle}</p></div>
        <span className="shrink-0 rounded-full bg-slate-200 px-3 py-0.5 text-xs font-bold">{st}</span></div>
      {s && <p className="muted mt-2">Best score {s.best}% Â· {s.attempts} attempt{s.attempts > 1 ? 's' : ''}</p>}</button></li>); })}</ul>);
}
export default function Course({ ctx }: { ctx: Ctx }) {
  const l = LEVELS.find(x => x.id === ctx.progress.currentLevel)!;
  const done = unitsOf(l.id).filter(u => ctx.progress.completed.includes(u.id)).length;
  return (<div className="space-y-4"><h1 className="text-2xl font-bold">My Course</h1><LevelSelector ctx={ctx} />
    <div className="card"><p className="font-semibold">{l.id} â€” {l.name}</p><p className="muted mb-3">{l.desc}</p><ProgressBar value={(done / UNITS_PER_LEVEL) * 100} label="Level progress" /><p className="muted mt-2">{done} of {UNITS_PER_LEVEL} units completed Â· {levelStatus(ctx, l.id)}</p></div>
    <UnitList ctx={ctx} level={l.id} /></div>);
}

import { useState } from 'react';
import type { Answer, Exercise } from '../types';
import { grade } from '../engine/grade';
import ProgressBar from './ProgressBar';

export const showAnswer = (ex: Exercise, a: Answer | undefined): string => {
  if (a === undefined) return 'â€”';
  switch (ex.type) {
    case 'multiple-choice': case 'reading-comprehension': return typeof a === 'number' ? ex.options?.[a] ?? 'â€”' : 'â€”';
    case 'true-false': return typeof a === 'boolean' ? (a ? 'True' : 'False') : 'â€”';
    case 'word-order': return Array.isArray(a) ? a.join(' ') : 'â€”';
    case 'matching': return typeof a === 'object' && !Array.isArray(a) ? Object.entries(a).map(([l, r]) => `${l} â†’ ${r}`).join(', ') : 'â€”';
    default: return typeof a === 'string' ? a : 'â€”';
  }
};
export const correctText = (ex: Exercise) =>
  ex.type === 'matching' ? (ex.pairs ?? []).map(([l, r]) => `${l} â†’ ${r}`).join(', ') : ex.type === 'short-answer' ? ex.rubric ?? '' : showAnswer(ex, ex.answer);
const opt = (on: boolean) => `block w-full min-h-[48px] rounded-lg border px-4 py-2 text-left ${on ? 'border-brand-600 bg-brand-50 font-semibold' : 'border-slate-300 bg-white hover:border-brand-600'} disabled:opacity-70`;

export function ExerciseView({ ex, value, onChange, locked, result }: { ex: Exercise; value: Answer | undefined; onChange: (a: Answer) => void; locked: boolean; result?: boolean | null }) {
  const picked = (Array.isArray(value) ? value : []) as string[];
  const remaining = [...(ex.words ?? [])];
  picked.forEach(w => { const i = remaining.indexOf(w); if (i >= 0) remaining.splice(i, 1); });
  const map = (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value) ? value : {}) as Record<string, string>;
  return (
    <div>
      <p className="muted">{ex.instructions}</p>
      {ex.passage && <p className="my-3 rounded-lg bg-slate-100 p-3 leading-relaxed">{ex.passage}</p>}
      <p className="my-3 text-lg font-semibold leading-snug">{ex.prompt}</p>
      {(ex.type === 'multiple-choice' || ex.type === 'reading-comprehension') && (
        <div className="space-y-2" role="radiogroup">{ex.options!.map((o, i) => <button key={o} role="radio" aria-checked={value === i} disabled={locked} className={opt(value === i)} onClick={() => onChange(i)}>{o}</button>)}</div>)}
      {ex.type === 'true-false' && <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-2">{[true, false].map(b => <button key={String(b)} disabled={locked} aria-pressed={value === b} className={opt(value === b)} onClick={() => onChange(b)}>{b ? 'True' : 'False'}</button>)}</div>}
      {(ex.type === 'fill-blank' || ex.type === 'sentence-transformation') && <input aria-label="Your answer" disabled={locked} value={typeof value === 'string' ? value : ''} onChange={e => onChange(e.target.value)} autoComplete="off" className="min-h-[48px] w-full rounded-lg border border-slate-300 px-3 text-base focus:border-brand-600 focus:outline-none focus:ring-1 focus:ring-brand-600" placeholder="Type your answer" />}
      {ex.type === 'short-answer' && <textarea aria-label="Your answer" disabled={locked} rows={4} value={typeof value === 'string' ? value : ''} onChange={e => onChange(e.target.value)} className="w-full rounded-lg border border-slate-300 p-3 focus:border-brand-600 focus:outline-none focus:ring-1 focus:ring-brand-600" placeholder="Write your answer here" />}
      {ex.type === 'word-order' && (
        <div>
          <div className="mb-3 flex min-h-[52px] flex-wrap gap-2 rounded-lg border border-dashed border-slate-400 p-2" aria-label="Your sentence">
            {picked.length === 0 && <span className="muted p-2">Tap the words below</span>}
            {picked.map((w, i) => <button key={i} disabled={locked} className="min-h-[40px] rounded-md bg-brand-600 px-3 text-white" onClick={() => onChange(picked.filter((_, j) => j !== i))}>{w}</button>)}
          </div>
          <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">{remaining.map((w, i) => <button key={i} disabled={locked} className="min-h-[40px] rounded-md border border-slate-300 bg-white px-3 hover:border-brand-600" onClick={() => onChange([...picked, w])}>{w}</button>)}</div>
        </div>)}
      {ex.type === 'matching' && <div className="space-y-2">{ex.pairs!.map(([l]) => (
        <label key={l} className="flex items-center justify-between gap-3"><span className="font-medium">{l}</span>
          <select disabled={locked} value={map[l] ?? ''} onChange={e => onChange({ ...map, [l]: e.target.value })} className="min-h-[44px] min-w-[150px] rounded-lg border border-slate-300 bg-white px-2">
            <option value="">Chooseâ€¦</option>{[...ex.pairs!.map(p => p[1])].sort().map(r => <option key={r}>{r}</option>)}</select></label>))}</div>}
      {result !== undefined && (
        <div role="status" className={`mt-4 rounded-lg border p-3 ${result === true ? 'border-emerald-300 bg-emerald-50' : result === false ? 'border-red-300 bg-red-50' : 'border-slate-300 bg-slate-50'}`}>
          <p className="font-semibold">{result === true ? 'Correct' : result === false ? 'Not quite' : 'Self-check'}</p>
          {result !== true && <p className="text-sm">{ex.type === 'short-answer' ? ex.rubric : <>Correct answer: <b>{correctText(ex)}</b></>}</p>}
          <p className="mt-1 text-sm">{ex.feedback}</p>
        </div>)}
    </div>
  );
}

const hasAnswer = (_ex: Exercise, a: Answer | undefined) => a !== undefined && !(Array.isArray(a) && a.length === 0) && (typeof a !== 'string' || a.trim() !== '');

export function ExerciseSet({ exercises, mode, onChecked, onFinish, finishLabel }: { exercises: Exercise[]; mode: 'practice' | 'test'; onChecked?: (ex: Exercise, ok: boolean | null) => void; onFinish?: (answers: Record<string, Answer>) => void; finishLabel?: string }) {
  const [i, setI] = useState(0);
  const [answers, setAnswers] = useState<Record<string, Answer>>({});
  const [checked, setChecked] = useState<Record<string, boolean | null>>({});
  const [done, setDone] = useState(false);
  const ex = exercises[i];
  if (done) {
    const auto = exercises.filter(e => e.type !== 'short-answer'), right = auto.filter(e => checked[e.id] === true).length;
    return <div className="card text-center"><p className="text-xl font-semibold">Practice finished</p><p className="my-2">{right} of {auto.length} auto-graded answers correct.</p>
      <button className="btn btn2" onClick={() => { setI(0); setAnswers({}); setChecked({}); setDone(false); }}>Practice again</button></div>;
  }
  const isChecked = ex.id in checked, last = i === exercises.length - 1;
  const check = () => { const r = grade(ex, answers[ex.id]); setChecked({ ...checked, [ex.id]: r }); onChecked?.(ex, r); };
  const next = () => { if (!last) setI(i + 1); else if (mode === 'test') onFinish?.(answers); else { setDone(true); onFinish?.(answers); } };
  return (
    <div className="card">
      <div className="mb-4"><div className="muted mb-1">Question {i + 1} of {exercises.length}</div><ProgressBar value={((i + 1) / exercises.length) * 100} label="Question progress" /></div>
      <ExerciseView key={ex.id} ex={ex} value={answers[ex.id]} onChange={a => setAnswers({ ...answers, [ex.id]: a })} locked={mode === 'practice' && isChecked} result={mode === 'practice' && isChecked ? checked[ex.id] : undefined} />
      <div className="mt-5 flex gap-2">
        {i > 0 && mode === 'test' && <button className="btn btn2" onClick={() => setI(i - 1)}>Back</button>}
        {mode === 'practice' && !isChecked && <button className="btn" disabled={!hasAnswer(ex, answers[ex.id])} onClick={check}>Check answer</button>}
        {(mode === 'test' || isChecked) && <button className="btn" onClick={next}>{last ? finishLabel ?? 'Finish' : 'Next'}</button>}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export default function ProgressBar({ value, label }: { value: number; label?: string }) {
  const v = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, value));
  return <div role="progressbar" aria-valuenow={v} aria-valuemin={0} aria-valuemax={100} aria-label={label ?? 'Progress'} className="h-2 overflow-hidden rounded bg-slate-200"><div className="h-full bg-brand-600 transition-all" style={{ width: `${v}%` }} /></div>;
}

    title: 'How to build an argument that holds together',
    text: 'A well-constructed essay is rarely a sequence of good ideas; it is a sequence of ideas that visibly depend on one another. This dependence, which linguists call cohesion, is created not merely by linking words such as â€œhoweverâ€ or â€œthereforeâ€, but also by the way each sentence begins with information already familiar to the reader and ends with something new. Writers who ignore this principle, producing sentences that introduce new material at the start, tend to leave their readers disoriented. Coherence, by contrast, concerns whether the text makes sense as a whole: whether the thesis is stated, supported and revisited, and whether every paragraph contributes to it. A frequent source of incoherence is the tendency to include material because it is interesting rather than because it is relevant. Academic conventions offer several remedies. Signposting, such as â€œThis section examinesâ€¦â€, tells readers what to expect; topic sentences announce the point of each paragraph; and nominalisation compresses actions into noun phrases, allowing complex relationships to be expressed concisely. Admittedly, over-use of such devices can produce prose that is dense and impersonal. The aim, ultimately, is not to impress but to be understood, which in academic writing usually means saying less, more precisely.',

We are told that we must choose between security and liberty, growth and the environment, tradition and progress, as though each pair marked the ends of a single road on which societies must locate themselves. The device is attractive precisely because it is economical: by reducing a complex question to two options, it spares the speaker the labour of justifying the many that have been excluded. It also flatters the audience, who are invited to see themselves as realists forced to choose the lesser evil. What is rarely acknowledged is that the framing does most of the argumentative work before any evidence is considered. Whoever defines the options largely determines the outcome. This is not to say that trade-offs do not exist; they plainly do. The point is rather that their existence does not entail that the available choices are limited to two, nor that the terms in which they are posed are neutral. A genuinely rigorous argument begins by interrogating the question: who benefits from this being posed as a choice between A and B, and what alternatives have quietly disappeared? Admittedly, such scrutiny is slower and less rhetorically satisfying than a confident ultimatum; it rarely fits into a headline.     title: 'Diplomacy is not the same as vagueness',
    text: 'In professional settings, diplomatic language is frequently mistaken for vagueness. A manager who tells a team that its report â€œhas some room for improvementâ€ believes herself to be tactful; the team, meanwhile, is left to guess whether the report needs a few corrections or a complete rewrite. The distinction matters, because diplomacy, properly understood, is a method of delivering a clear message in a form the listener can accept, not a way of avoiding the message altogether. Linguists have noted that certain expressions function as softeners rather than as blurring devices: â€œI wonder whether it might be worth reconsidering the timelineâ€ is, in context, a recommendation, and is generally understood as such. Problems arise when the softening becomes so elaborate that the recommendation is lost, or when it is applied selectively, so that colleagues learn to read the strongest criticism into the mildest remark. Cultures differ here, too: a formulation that in one environment signals polite disagreement may, in another, be taken as agreement. Skilled leaders therefore calibrate. They are explicit where the stakes are high or the timeline short, and more tentative where they genuinely wish to invite alternatives. Above all, they are consistent, so that their words acquire a predictable weight. It would be a mistake, then, to regard directness and diplomacy as opposites. Sentences such as â€œThe measures are widely believed to have backfiredâ€ or â€œThe firm is said to have ignored warningsâ€ present a judgement as common knowledge while leaving the source conveniently unnamed. The device is not necessarily deceptive; journalists often use it when a source cannot be identified for legitimate reasons. But a reader who takes such formulations at face value is accepting, on trust, a claim that has not been supported. Scholars of media language therefore advise a simple discipline: when a report attributes, ask who is attributing, and with what verb. Neutral verbs are rarer than we imagine, and when they appear, it is worth asking what has been left out. This is not an argument for cynicism. The pattern is not limited to colonial anecdotes: schools judged by exam results may be tempted to discourage weaker pupils from sitting them, and hospitals judged on waiting times may reclassify patients rather than treat them sooner. Much of it, however, comes from habits that have nothing to do with complexity: sentences that begin with long abstract subjects, nominalisations stacked on one another, and paragraphs in which each statement is true but none seems to follow from the last. Research on readability suggests that readers cope best when each sentence begins with familiar material and reserves its novelty for the end, and when abstract nouns are tethered to concrete actors. â€œThe implementation of the evaluation of the programmeâ€ asks the reader to translate it back into a story; â€œthe team evaluated the programmeâ€ does not. The problem arises when it is used by default, so that actors vanish and every process becomes a thing. A sound rule of thumb is to nominalise when the noun phrase will serve as a stable reference in later sentences, and to retain the verb when the reader needs to know who did what. Writers who follow such principles do not abandon the formal register; they use it with greater control. What distinguishes them is not the absence of such events but the ease with which they are managed. A fluent speaker who loses a word describes around it; one who misjudges the register of a remark adjusts the next; one who realises that a listener has not followed rephrases without condescension. These are strategies, and strategies, unlike accuracy in the narrow sense, can be taught and practised. They also explain why fluency varies with context: the same person may be commanding in a seminar on their specialism and halting in a conversation about plumbing, since the lexical resources that sustain fluency are unevenly distributed. The trouble lies in the assumption on which such lists rest, that meaning is a single thing which words either share or lack. In practice, a word carries several kinds of information at once. It has a denotation, but also a register, an evaluative tilt, a set of habitual partners and, sometimes, a regional flavour that the dictionary entry does not mention. Two words may overlap on the first and differ on all the others. â€œSlimâ€ and â€œskinnyâ€ describe the same silhouette; the speaker who chooses between them is also choosing between admiration and criticism. â€œObstinateâ€ and â€œtenaciousâ€ describe the same refusal to yield, but one is a reproach and the other, in the right reference letter, a compliment. It does not follow that the solution is to acquire more vocabulary. The more useful discipline is to attend to the company words keep, to notice what a word is usually used to praise, to blame or to soften, and to prefer, when in doubt, the common word whose behaviour one knows to the exotic one whose behaviour one has merely read about. Precision, in this sense, is less a matter of range than of respect: for the way in which a language has, over generations, decided what its words are for.',

=== FILE: C:\Users\Admin\Downloads\english-path-source\english-path\src\engine\grade.ts ===
import type { Answer, Exercise } from '../types';
export const norm = (s: string) =>
  s.toLowerCase().replace(/[â€™â€˜]/g, "'").trim().replace(/[.!?Â¿Â¡,]+$/g, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
const same = (a: string[], b: string[]) => a.length === b.length && a.every((x, i) => x === b[i]);

/** true/false = auto-graded; null = open answer (self-check against rubric, never auto-scored). */
export function grade(ex: Exercise, a: Answer | undefined): boolean | null {
  if (ex.type === 'short-answer') return null;
  if (a === undefined || a === '' || (Array.isArray(a) && a.length === 0)) return false;
  switch (ex.type) {
    case 'multiple-choice': case 'reading-comprehension': case 'true-false': return a === ex.answer;
    case 'fill-blank': case 'sentence-transformation': {
      const ok = [ex.answer as string, ...(ex.accept ?? [])].map(norm);
      return typeof a === 'string' && ok.includes(norm(a));
    }
    case 'word-order': return Array.isArray(a) && same(a.map(norm), (ex.answer as string[]).map(norm));
    case 'matching': {
      const m = a as Record<string, string>;
      return !!ex.pairs && ex.pairs.every(([l, r]) => m[l] === r);
    }
  }
}
export const pct = (right: number, total: number) => (total ? Math.round((right / total) * 100) : 0);
export const PASS = 80;
export function studyTip(score: number): string {
  if (score >= 95) return 'Excellent. Move on to the next unit and keep using these structures in speaking and writing.';
  if (score >= PASS) return 'Good work. Read the explanations for the questions you missed, then continue.';
  if (score >= 50) return 'Review the Grammar and Vocabulary sections, redo the practice exercises, and retake the assessment.';
  return 'Go back to Objectives, Grammar and the Dialogue. Study them slowly, then try the exercises again before the assessment.';
}

import type { Level, Progress, Score, Settings } from '../types';
const KEY = 'englishpath.progress.v1', SKEY = 'englishpath.settings.v1';
export const defaultProgress = (): Progress => ({ currentLevel: 'A1', currentUnit: null, completed: [], reviewUnits: [], scores: {}, practice: {}, savedVocab: [], activity: [], lastActivity: null });
export const defaultSettings = (): Settings => ({ showTranslations: true });
type Store = { getItem(k: string): string | null; setItem(k: string, v: string): void };
const ls = (): Store | null => { try { return (globalThis as any).localStorage ?? null; } catch { return null; } };
export function load<T>(key: string, def: () => T): T {
  try { const raw = ls()?.getItem(key); return raw ? { ...def(), ...JSON.parse(raw) } : def(); } catch { return def(); }
}
export const loadProgress = () => load(KEY, defaultProgress);
export const loadSettings = () => load(SKEY, defaultSettings);
function save(key: string, v: unknown) { try { ls()?.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(v)); } catch { /* storage unavailable: app keeps working in memory */ } }
export const saveProgress = (p: Progress) => save(KEY, p);
export const saveSettings = (s: Settings) => save(SKEY, s);

const stamp = (p: Progress, text: string): Progress => {
  const at = new Date().toISOString();
  return { ...p, lastActivity: at, activity: [{ at, text }, ...p.activity].slice(0, 20) };
};
export const openUnit = (p: Progress, level: Level, unitId: string, title: string): Progress =>
  stamp({ ...p, currentLevel: level, currentUnit: unitId }, `Opened ${title}`);
export function recordPractice(p: Progress, unitId: string, exId: string, ok: boolean): Progress {
  const done = new Set(p.practice[unitId] ?? []);
  if (ok) done.add(exId); else done.delete(exId);
  return { ...p, practice: { ...p.practice, [unitId]: [...done] } };
}
export function recordAssessment(p: Progress, unitId: string, title: string, score: number, passed: boolean): Progress {
  const old: Score | undefined = p.scores[unitId];
  const scores = { ...p.scores, [unitId]: { best: Math.max(old?.best ?? 0, score), last: score, attempts: (old?.attempts ?? 0) + 1, date: new Date().toISOString() } };
  const completed = passed ? [...new Set([...p.completed, unitId])] : p.completed;
  const reviewUnits = passed ? p.reviewUnits.filter(u => u !== unitId) : [...new Set([...p.reviewUnits, unitId])];
  return stamp({ ...p, scores, completed, reviewUnits }, `${title}: ${score}% â€” ${passed ? 'COMPLETED' : 'REVIEW'}`);
}
export function toggleVocab(p: Progress, key: string): Progress {
  const has = p.savedVocab.includes(key);
  return { ...p, savedVocab: has ? p.savedVocab.filter(k => k !== key) : [...p.savedVocab, key] };
}
/** Resets progress only. Course content lives in src/data and is never touched. */
export const resetProgress = (): Progress => defaultProgress();
